name: python-engineering
description: Use when writing, reviewing or tuning Python: performance, GIL and free-threading, subinterpreters, gRPC, message queues, caches, typing and tooling.
title: Python engineering
goal: Write code that is correct first, then fast, with measurements to prove it.
steps: Read `{{skill_dir}}/references/python.md` for the sections that match the task (clean code, performance, concurrency, architecture-specific work).
Look at the project first: version, dependencies, existing style, tests, how it is built and run. Follow its conventions.
For a performance task: write or find a benchmark, record the baseline, profile, change one thing, re-measure. Report before and after numbers with the command that produced them.
Run the project's formatter, linter and tests. Report what you ran and the results; if you could not run something, say so.
State what you did not verify (other platforms, other versions, production load).
output: The change or review, with the evidence: commands run, benchmark numbers before and after, and a short list of risks and unverified points.
gotchas: Never claim a speedup without a measurement from this code.
Version-specific claims must be checked against the version in use.
